_meta.description: Authoritative reference for every push notification type in the PPF app. Uses Supabase + direct APNs/FCM — NO Firebase SDK on the device. Defines the payload shape, the Supabase edge function that fires it, and the in-app deep-link target (tab + context) that the mobile app navigates to on tap.

implementation_stack.NO_firebase: Firebase SDK is NOT used anywhere in this project. Do not add @react-native-firebase.
implementation_stack.auth_and_db: Supabase Auth + Supabase PostgREST (already in place)
implementation_stack.device_library: @notifee/react-native — handles notification display, channels, badges, foreground notifications, tap events. Works with raw APNs/FCM tokens.
implementation_stack.ios_token: PushNotificationIOS (React Native built-in) or Notifee.requestPermission() → returns raw APNs device token
implementation_stack.android_token: FCM HTTP v1 API still required for Android delivery — but called SERVER-SIDE only from Supabase edge functions. The mobile app gets an FCM registration token via @react-native-community/push-notification-ios on iOS and react-native built-ins on Android (without the full Firebase SDK, use the lightweight @react-native-firebase/messaging standalone module OR use Notifee which supports direct token registration).
implementation_stack.recommended_mobile_setup: @notifee/react-native (display) + react-native PushNotificationIOS (iOS APNs token registration) + react-native VapidPush / direct FCM token on Android

server_side_delivery.ios: Supabase Edge Function → APNs HTTP/2 API directly using JWT (ES256) signed with the .p8 key. No Firebase involved.
server_side_delivery.android: Supabase Edge Function → FCM HTTP v1 API (https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/messages:send) using a Google service account JWT. This is a direct Google API call — no Firebase SDK on the device.

implementation_stack.badge_source: Supabase Realtime subscription on messages table + get_unread_count RPC

push_token_registration.description: How the mobile app registers device tokens and stores them in Supabase — no Firebase SDK involved.
flow: 1. On login (AuthContext user set), call notifee.requestPermission()
2. iOS: listen to PushNotificationIOS.addEventListener('register', token => ...) to get the raw APNs device token (hex string)

3. Android: call messaging().getToken() from the lightweight standalone @react-native-firebase/messaging (OR use Notifee's FCM token helper — this is NOT the full Firebase SDK, just the FCM token fetcher)
4. PATCH profiles SET push_token = <token>, push_platform = 'ios'|'android' WHERE id = user.id (using existing restPatch from restClient.ts)
5. iOS: also listen to PushNotificationIOS.addEventListener('registrationError') for token failures
6. Re-register on every app foreground (tokens can rotate silently on iOS)
7. On signOut: PATCH profiles SET push_token = null, push_platform = null
push_token_registration.ios_entitlement_required: aps-environment (development | production) — set in Xcode Signing & Capabilities → Push Notifications

in_app_notification_handler.description: How App.tsx handles notification taps to navigate to the right screen — all handled via @notifee, no Firebase

logic.foreground_tap: useEffect(() => notifee.onForegroundEvent(({ type, detail }) => { if (type === EventType.PRESS) handleNotificationTap(detail.notification.data) }), [])
logic.killed_state_tap: notifee.getInitialNotification() → handleNotificationTap on mount if present
logic.foreground_display: When app is open, DO NOT show OS alert for new_message if that conversation is already open. Otherwise show an in-app banner via notifee.displayNotification() with a custom Android channel.
logic.supabase_realtime_fallback: For foreground message badge updates, use Supabase Realtime channel subscription on messages table (recipient_id=eq.{userId}) — no push needed when app is open.

badge_management.description: How the app badge count (red dot on home screen icon) is managed

clear_on.Messages tab open: notifee.setBadgeCount(0) + mark messages as read via Supabase
clear_on.Specific conversation open: Decrement badge by that conversation's unread count

badge_management.server_sync: Call Supabase RPC get_unread_count on app foreground → returns { messages: N, orders: N, total: N } → notifee.setBadgeCount(total)
badge_management.tab_bar_badge: TabBar receives unreadMessages prop (currently hardcoded 0 in App.tsx line 55 — wire to unreadCount state from usePushNotifications hook)

server_side_delivery.description: How Supabase edge functions send notifications directly to APNs and FCM — no Firebase SDK, no Firebase console

ios_apns.auth: JWT signed with ES256 using the .p8 private key. Header: { alg: 'ES256', kid: APNS_KEY_ID }. Claims: { iss: APNS_TEAM_ID, iat: now }. Token is reused for up to 59 minutes.
ios_apns.deno_helper: supabase/functions/_shared/apns.ts — signs JWT with Deno crypto.subtle, sends fetch to APNs HTTP/2 endpoint

android_fcm.auth: OAuth2 access token from Google service account JWT (NOT the old FCM server key — v1 API requires OAuth2). Sign a JWT with the service account private key, exchange for access token.
android_fcm.note: You need a Firebase project ONLY to get FCM credentials for Android delivery. No Firebase SDK goes on the device. The service account JSON is stored as a Supabase secret.
android_fcm.deno_helper: supabase/functions/_shared/fcm.ts — generates Google OAuth2 token and POSTs to FCM v1 API

server_side_delivery.shared_send_function: supabase/functions/_shared/sendPush.ts — takes { token, platform, title, body, data } → routes to apns.ts or fcm.ts based on platform

secrets_required.description: All stored via `supabase secrets set KEY=value` — nothing in .env files

supabase_secrets.APNS_KEY_ID: 10-char key ID from Apple Developer Portal (e.g. ABC1234567)
supabase_secrets.APNS_TEAM_ID: 10-char Apple Team ID from developer.apple.com top-right
supabase_secrets.APNS_PRIVATE_KEY: Full contents of the .p8 file with newlines as \n  — NEVER commit this file
supabase_secrets.APNS_BUNDLE_ID: Your iOS bundle ID e.g. com.ppf.mobile
supabase_secrets.FCM_PROJECT_ID: Firebase project ID (for FCM v1 API endpoint path only — no SDK on device)
supabase_secrets.FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: Full Google service account JSON as a single-line string — used to get OAuth2 token for FCM v1 API

NOT_needed: No Firebase SDK initialization in App.tsx

apns_setup_checklist: [ ] Apple Developer Portal → Certificates, IDs & Profiles → Keys → + → enable Apple Push Notifications service (APNs)
[ ] Download the .p8 key file — CAN ONLY BE DOWNLOADED ONCE. Store in 1Password/vault immediately.
[ ] Note Key ID (10 chars shown after creation) and Team ID (top-right corner of developer.apple.com)
[ ] In Xcode: change bundle ID from org.reactjs.native.example.PPFMobile to your production ID (e.g. com.ppf.mobile)
[ ] In Xcode: Signing & Capabilities → + Capability → Push Notifications
[ ] In Xcode: Signing & Capabilities → + Capability → Background Modes → check 'Remote notifications'
[ ] Run: supabase secrets set APNS_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX APNS_TEAM_ID=XXXXXXXXXX APNS_BUNDLE_ID=com.ppf.mobile
[ ] Run: supabase secrets set APNS_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 | tr '\n' '|' | sed 's/|/\\n/g')"
[ ] For Android FCM: create Firebase project (push delivery only — no SDK on device), create service account, download JSON
[ ] Run: supabase secrets set FCM_PROJECT_ID=your-project-id FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON='<json string>'

database_webhooks_setup.description: How to connect Supabase DB events to edge functions — done in Supabase Dashboard → Database → Webhooks
database_webhooks_setup.authentication: Each webhook call includes Authorization: Bearer {SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY} header — verify in edge function

testing.simulator: APNs does NOT work on iOS Simulator — must use a real physical device for push testing
testing.ios_sandbox: Development builds use APNs sandbox endpoint: https://api.sandbox.push.apple.com. Set APNS_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox secret for dev, production for prod.
testing.manual_test: POST directly to the edge function with a test payload: curl -X POST https://{project}.supabase.co/functions/v1/notify-new-message -H 'Authorization: Bearer {service_role_key}' -d '{"record":{"recipient_id":"USER_UUID","content":"Test"}}'
testing.token_logging: In usePushNotifications.ts, console.log the device token on registration so you can test-fire via curl
testing.notifee_local_test: notifee.displayNotification({ title: 'Test', body: 'Hello', data: { ppf_type: 'new_message', conversation_id: 'xxx' } }) — tests the tap handler without a real push
